description: The SPECIAL-NAMES ORDER TABLE ordering-name-1 IS literal-9 clause, ISO 12.3.7.2 (the last item of the paragraph's general format) - introduced 2002 with the cultural-ordering facility. Literal-9 identifies a cultural ordering table constructed per ISO/IEC 14651:2020 Annex A and the implementor specifies its allowable content (12.3.7.4 GR17); ordering-name-1 may be specified only in the STANDARD-COMPARE intrinsic function (12.3.7.3 SR9). Parse-arm gated on recognition (VisitOrderTableClause). The grammar predicate is NOT edition-gated, unlike the LOCALE clause's: TABLE is reserved at every edition (reserved-words.json r85 true), so the pair ORDER + TABLE has no competing COBOL-85 reading, and recognizing it everywhere is what makes the sub-2002 answer this explanatory COBOL0900 instead of a parse error at TABLE.
citation: ISO §2023:12.3.7.2 (the ORDER TABLE clause of the SPECIAL-NAMES general format); §2023:12.3.7.3 SR9/SR10/SR11; §2023:12.3.7.4 GR17
vcr: 2002 introduction (the cultural-ordering facility; kb/Work PB101 - ORDER TABLE + STANDARD-COMPARE over the derived CLDR/UCA collation engine). Annex E covers 2014-2023 only, so the 2002 edge is derived from the ORDER reserved-word row (reserved-words.json r85 false / r2002 true), not from an E-list entry.
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. PB101OT.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
CONFIGURATION SECTION.
SPECIAL-NAMES.
    ORDER TABLE OT1 IS "ISO 14651_2020_TABLE1".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    STOP RUN.
